fixes.explanation: Forty years, baker. Moses says the LORD “…made them wander in the wilderness forty years, until the whole generation who had done evil in His sight was gone.” (Numbers 32:13). Forty years is a long time to wander. I think this part of the story is a heavy one.

Vineyards, huh? Somebody was picturing grape juice on their apron. Here the Reubenites and Gadites have very large herds and flocks, and they look over Jazer and Gilead and see land suitable for livestock (Numbers 32:1). The verse leaves the grapes out. Their minds are on the animals.

False is right, baker. Moses says, “But if you do not do this, you will certainly sin against the LORD—and be assured that your sin will find you out.” (Numbers 32:23). So nobody gets to slip by unnoticed. The words are very plain.

Time to think it over? No, baker, no stalling here. Moses says to build the cities and folds, but do what they promised (Numbers 32:24). They answer right away: “Your servants will do just as our lord commands.” (Numbers 32:25). I've stood over a cooling rack taking longer to decide on a cookie than these two tribes take to say yes.

Put them to work? That's not what the verse reports, baker. It says the descendants of Machir son of Manasseh “…went to Gilead, captured it, and drove out the Amorites who were there.” (Numbers 32:39). The text tells us they drove them out. It says nothing about the Amorites doing any work for them.
